title: Dorset named among the most haunted road hotspots in the UK with 51 reports
excerpt: Dorset named UK haunted road hotspot with 51 paranormal reports, as cinch research ranks Wiltshire first and reveals ghostly figures and phantom hitchhikers.
content:
Dorset has been named the UK’s second-biggest haunted road hotspot after 51 paranormal reports were linked to roads across the county, according to new research released ahead of Halloween. (Image: Daily Echo)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

Dorset has been named one of the most haunted road hotspots in the UK, with 51 reports of paranormal activity.

The findings come from research by Cinch, the UK’s biggest online used car retailer, which analysed reports from The Paranormal Database’s Roads and Motorways archive.

Wiltshire topped the list with 57 reports, followed by Dorset with 51 and Essex with 50.

Other counties in the top 5 include Suffolk with 45 and Somerset with 43.

Ben Welham, motoring expert at Cinch, said: "Whether you believe in ghosts or not, seeing something you can’t explain while you’re driving would be enough to catch anyone off guard.

"Some of the stories have been around for decades, while others have been submitted much more recently, so it’s clear they still capture people’s imagination.

"It’ll be interesting to see if any new sightings are reported this Halloween."

Haunted road sightings include ghostly figures, phantom hitchhikers, unexplained animals, and disappearing vehicles.

In Wiltshire, reports include a horse and rider vanishing into a wall on the A365 and a grinning, skull-faced figure on the A4 near Corsham.

The south west leads the UK in haunted road sightings, with 218 in total.

The full ranking can be found at the Cinch website.
